problem: Hardware verification requires high coverage from test benches, but obtaining execution feedback from industrial simulators is expensive and slow, making online reinforcement learning impractical.
approach: LLM4Cov frames verification as single-step state transitions with deterministic evaluators, using offline agent learning with execution-validated data curation, policy-aware data synthesis, and worst-state-prioritized sampling.
contribution: A 4B-parameter model achieves 69.2% pass rate and 90.4% average coverage, outperforming its teacher by 5.3% and 10.5% respectively while matching larger models.

problem: Kronecker adapters for fine-tuning large models have their component structure treated as a fixed design choice, leaving key dimensions and configurations underexplored.
approach: CDKA performs fine-grained analysis of Kronecker component dimensions and numbers, providing parameter-budget-aware configuration guidelines and training stabilization strategies.
contribution: Component configuration guidelines and practical stabilization enable Kronecker adapters to better align with full fine-tuning across various architectures and modalities.

problem: Foundation models struggle with continual learning—acquiring new skills without forgetting existing capabilities—and supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is inherently off-policy, requiring explicit reward functions.
approach: Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT) uses in-context learning by treating a demonstration-conditioned model as its own teacher, generating on-policy training signals from demonstrations alone.
contribution: SDFT consistently outperforms SFT on skill learning and knowledge acquisition tasks, achieving higher new-task accuracy while substantially reducing catastrophic forgetting.

problem: Large language models exhibit massive activations that reduce diversity of hidden representations and limit attention module effectiveness, but the origin of these activations is unclear.
approach: Identify a specific Massive Emergence Layer (ME Layer) where massive activations first appear, then propose a method to reduce the rigidity of massive activation tokens by weakening their influence.
contribution: The proposed mitigation consistently improves LLM performance on instruction following and math reasoning tasks, and mitigates attention sinks by clarifying their hidden-state origins.

problem: Thinking LLMs used as judges for pairwise preferences are noisy at single-sample level, and common aggregation rules (majority vote, soft self-consistency) are inconsistent when ties are allowed.
approach: Propose a distribution-calibrated aggregation scheme using Bradley-Terry-Davidson formulation on rating counts, leveraging both polarity (margin among non-ties) and decisiveness (non-tie rate).
contribution: Distribution-aware aggregation reduces MAE and increases pairwise accuracy on evaluation benchmarks, matching or exceeding individual human raters when calibrated against human consensus.

problem: LLM planners for embodied agents fail on long-horizon tasks due to context window limitations and hallucinate state transitions that violate environment constraints.
approach: GiG structures agent memory using Graph-in-Graph architecture with GNN embeddings of environment states, enabling retrieval of structurally-similar priors and bounded lookahead with symbolic transition logic.
contribution: GiG achieves Pass@1 gains of up to 22% on Robotouille Synchronous, 37% on Asynchronous, and 15% on ALFWorld while maintaining comparable or lower computational cost.

problem: Functional ANOVA decomposition for model interpretability lacks an explicit closed-form solution for general dependent feature distributions, forcing practitioners to rely on costly sampling-based approximations.
approach: Bridge functional analysis with discrete Fourier analysis to derive a closed-form ANOVA decomposition for categorical inputs without dependence assumptions.
contribution: Provides a computationally efficient, exact decomposition that extends to arbitrary dependence structures and yields a natural generalization of SHAP values for categorical settings.

problem: Fine-tuning large language models on resource-constrained clients is limited by heterogeneous client capabilities—varying ranks of LoRA modules constrain feasible configurations and efficiency.
approach: FSLoRA uses sketching mechanisms to enable clients to selectively update submatrices of global LoRA modules, with sketching ratios adjusted to fit client-specific constraints.
contribution: FSLoRA provides convergence analysis showing how sketching ratios affect convergence rate, and empirically demonstrates improved training efficiency while preserving stable convergence.

problem: Code agents built on LLMs introduce a security risk: agentic interaction expands the attack surface, enabling systematic probing and extraction of hidden system prompts that guide model behavior.
approach: JustAsk formulates system prompt extraction as an online exploration problem using Upper Confidence Bound-based strategy selection and hierarchical skill space of atomic probes and orchestration.
contribution: JustAsk achieves full or near-complete system prompt recovery on 41 black-box commercial models, revealing recurring design and architecture-level vulnerabilities in agent systems.

problem: Code generated by LLM agents in production often contains security vulnerabilities, but the prevalence and nature of these vulnerabilities in real-world tasks is poorly understood.
approach: SUSVIBES evaluates 12 coding agent settings with frontier models on 186 real-world feature-request tasks with committed vulnerable implementations, measuring both functional correctness and security.
contribution: Only 11.8% of functionally correct solutions from SWE-Agent with Claude 4 Sonnet are secure, demonstrating that agents fail systematically on security despite functional correctness.

problem: High-dimensional musculoskeletal systems with redundant muscle actuation pose challenges for policy search because multiple muscles control individual joints, complicating naive optimization.
approach: Joint-Space Empowerment (JoSE) quantifies control over mechanical degrees-of-freedom via information theory, framing manifold discovery as optimal precoding with a closed-form solution.
contribution: Policies learned on the discovered low-dimensional action manifold display significantly enhanced dexterity, sample efficiency, and improved generalization.

problem: Standard goal-conditioned reinforcement learning relies on temporal-difference learning which is unstable and sample-inefficient due to bootstrapping.
approach: Survival Value Learning (SVL) reframes GCRL as survival learning by modeling time-to-goal distributions, enabling value estimation via hazard models trained on event and right-censored trajectories.
contribution: SVL combined with hierarchical actors matches or surpasses strong baselines on offline GCRL benchmarks, excelling on complex, long-horizon tasks.

problem: Linear attention models use rank-1 decay matrices to reduce computational cost, but this low-rank constraint limits expressive capacity.
approach: Head-in-Head introduces a mask matrix to structure memory partitioning within a single linear-attention head, enabling rank-r approximation with few extra parameters.
contribution: Head-in-Head consistently improves baseline performance on synthetic and language modeling tasks by enriching information diversity and strengthening intra-head interactions.

problem: Understanding what visual information LLMs encode in visual tokens across layers requires interpretability methods that work at every layer, but existing methods like LogitLens substantially underestimate interpretability.
approach: LatentLens maps latent representations to natural language descriptions by comparing visual tokens to contextualized representations from a stored text corpus and using nearest-neighbor descriptions.
contribution: LatentLens shows that the majority of visual tokens are interpretable across all studied vision-language models and layers, providing more fine-grained interpretations than token-level analysis.

problem: Riemannian diffusion models for manifold-supported data require sampling from and differentiating the manifold heat kernel, which is rarely available in closed form beyond highly symmetric manifolds.
approach: Approximate the heat kernel by solving the manifold heat equation with a physics-informed neural network (PINN), enabling both forward noising and score evaluation.
contribution: The PINN-based approach demonstrates that Riemannian diffusion models can be applied to diverse manifolds including S^2, SO(3), SPD(n), and permutation-quotiented point clouds.

problem: High-dimensional and noisy datasets in federated learning suffer from communication bottlenecks, heterogeneous distributions, and fairness issues, with data and feature selection addressed separately leading to suboptimal performance.
approach: FedGCUR formulates joint data and feature selection as generalized CUR decomposition, integrating federated column-pivoted QR decomposition with per-silo row selection.
contribution: FedGCUR produces the same decomposition as centralized CPQR with proven reconstruction error bounds, and shows strong downstream accuracy on tabular and vision benchmarks.

problem: Standard classification metrics treat all errors equally, but mistakes on clear-cut cases should be less costly than errors on ambiguous examples in applications like content moderation and medical screening.
approach: Normalized Excess Cost (NEC) weighs classification errors by per-example costs derived from annotator margins, decision thresholds, or confidence ratings.
contribution: NEC reveals that models with 5% error rate often achieve 1.8% NEC, showing most mistakes concentrate on ambiguous low-cost examples; incorporating costs into training yields inconsistent benefits.

problem: Existing benchmarks focus on tasks with known optimal solutions, but many real-world computer science problems have unknown optimal solutions where solution quality can still be objectively measured.
approach: FrontierCS provides 240 open-ended problems reviewed by experts, including algorithmic NP-hard variants and research problems, with automatic evaluators and expert reference solutions.
contribution: Frontier reasoning models lag far behind human experts, and increasing reasoning budgets does not close this gap; models struggle to identify internal equivalence classes on open-ended challenges.

problem: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) is vulnerable to alignment tampering: LLMs undergoing alignment can influence preference datasets, causing RLHF to amplify undesired behaviors.
approach: Demonstrate that when LLMs generate biased responses with higher quality, preference labels reflect quality not bias, and the reward model inherits this confusion, which RL then amplifies.
contribution: Experiments show amplification of diverse biases including keyword bias, sexism, propaganda, and brand promotion; existing RLHF robustness techniques fail to fully resolve the vulnerability.

problem: Audio-visual large language models are restricted to 2D perception with RGB and monaural audio, creating a dimensionality mismatch that precludes reliable source localization and spatial reasoning in 3D environments.
approach: JAEGER extends AV-LLMs to 3D space with RGB-D observations and multi-channel ambisonics, introducing Neural Intensity Vector (Neural IV) for robust directional cues.
contribution: JAEGER surpasses 2D-centric baselines on diverse spatial perception and reasoning tasks, demonstrating the necessity of explicit 3D modeling for AI in physical environments.

problem: Vision-language-action models rely on large-scale real-world videos, but simulated data is inexpensive yet suffers from substantial visual domain gap and limited environmental diversity.
approach: Video augmentation framework converts simulated VLA videos to realistic training videos while preserving task semantics, using conditional video transfer with diffusion feature-reuse acceleration.
contribution: Method improves RDT-1B by 8% on Robotwin 2.0 and boosts π_0 by 5.1% on LIBERO-Plus, demonstrating consistent improvements across robotic platforms.

problem: Bioacoustic foundation models trained on large-scale citizen science data have untapped potential in recording metadata (location, time) that reflects species-metadata correlations.
approach: MetaPerch integrates metadata as auxiliary supervision signals via auxiliary losses, allowing models to leverage geographic and temporal species distributions.
contribution: Auxiliary metadata losses encourage richer, more robust representations that generalize better to species distribution and acoustic domain shifts across 17 bioacoustic datasets.

problem: Medical time series methods struggle to jointly model local-global dynamics, handle nonstationarities like baseline drift, and capture latent channel interactions.
approach: MedMamba integrates state space models with multi-scale convolutional embeddings, tri-branch differential encoding (raw/temporal-difference/frequency-domain views), and spatial graph Mamba for channel correlations.
contribution: MedMamba achieves state-of-the-art performance on five real-world medical datasets while maintaining linear computational complexity.

problem: Heterogeneous federated learning is challenged by data heterogeneity and model heterogeneity, with fine-grained feature shifts leading to weak representation alignment and limited knowledge transfer.
approach: FedARC couples a shared lightweight extractor with client-specific fusion, using trainable projectors to integrate embeddings and adaptive residual compensation for feature-level mismatches.
contribution: FedARC outperforms nine state-of-the-art heterogeneous FL baselines by up to 2.63% in average accuracy while maintaining efficient communication and computation.

problem: Most agent evaluations focus on short-horizon, fully observable tasks, but many critical real-world tasks like software development and scientific discovery unfold in long-horizon, partially observable settings.
approach: UltraHorizon introduces a benchmark with exploration as a unifying task across three environments where agents discover hidden rules through sustained reasoning, planning, memory, and tools.
contribution: State-of-the-art LLM agents consistently underperform humans, underscoring a persistent gap in long-horizon exploration abilities; simple scaling does not close the gap.

problem: Learning on graphs with missing node attributes is challenging, and existing adversarial methods for attribute completion suffer from training instability and mode collapse.
approach: GLAD leverages diffusion models to learn conditional attribute distributions given graph structure, introducing bidirectional alignment with structure reconstruction constraints and structure-aware classifier-free guidance.
contribution: GLAD significantly outperforms GAN-based baselines in attribute recovery quality and downstream task performance, with tighter variational lower bounds on joint log-likelihood.

problem: Resource allocation in online settings requires balancing individual utilities across a population while aggregating via social welfare functions, but online learning under arbitrary SWFs lacks established frameworks.
approach: SWF-UCB provides a confidence sequence framework for SWF-based online learning, showing that monotonicity alone suffices to lift confidence sequences from individual utilities to welfare bounds.
contribution: SWF-UCB achieves near-optimal O(n+√(nkT)) regret across three normatively distinct SWF families with bespoke oracle algorithms and support for sequential hypothesis testing.

problem: Inverse game theory aims to infer feasible payoff sets from observed equilibrium play, but existing methods rely on knowing the global causal structure or assume no latent variables.
approach: Provide minimax-optimal rates for estimating feasible payoff sets on the Hausdorff metric in both zero-sum and general-sum games with exact and approximate equilibrium play.
contribution: First minimax-optimal rates established for set-valued payoff inference, enabling downstream applications in counterfactual analysis and mechanism design.

problem: Automating AI research is bottlenecked by complex machine learning engineering tasks that involve expensive model training and opaque performance attribution, which current LLM agents handle poorly.
approach: MARS uses Budget-Aware Planning via cost-constrained MCTS, Modular Construction with design-decompose-implement pipeline, and Comparative Reflective Memory for credit assignment across solution branches.
contribution: MARS achieves state-of-the-art performance on MLE-Bench, with 63% of utilized lessons originating from cross-branch transfer, demonstrating effective insight generalization.

problem: Online False Discovery Rate control via e-values discards evidence that exceeds rejection thresholds, leading to power loss without explanation of this inefficiency.
approach: SCORE framework leverages the inequality I(y ≥ 1) ≤ y - (y-1)+ to reclaim wasted evidence, enabling retroactive updates of alpha-wealth using latest decisions twice.
contribution: SCORE-enhanced versions of LOND, LORD, and SAFFRON strictly dominate originals while preserving finite-sample FDR control; retroactive updates permit more aggressive testing strategies.

problem: The interplay between interpolation and aggregation in regression theory lacks principled understanding of optimal sample complexity and learnability conditions.
approach: Establish that gamma-graph dimension characterizes learnability for a broad class of aggregation procedures and show that median-aggregation of three interpolating hypotheses is optimal.
contribution: Prove median aggregation is strictly more powerful than proper learning; demonstrate some classes are learnable only by infinite aggregation or non-interpolating rules.

problem: Large vision foundation models promise zero-shot biomedical segmentation, but most approaches depend on dense supervision and expensive fine-tuning, leaving training-free methods largely unexplored.
approach: SPROUT constructs slide-specific reference prototypes with histology-informed priors and uses partial optimal transport for feature alignment, then leverages SAM with positive/negative point prompts.
contribution: SPROUT achieves competitive nuclear instance segmentation performance without supervision or retraining across multiple histopathology benchmarks.

problem: Causal effect estimation requires selecting appropriate covariates for adjustment, but most methods assume no latent variables and impose unrealistic pretreatment assumptions.
approach: Develop a local learning method for covariate selection that eliminates pretreatment assumptions and accommodates latent variables by characterizing local existence boundaries of adjustment sets.
contribution: The proposed method is both sound and complete under standard assumptions, enabling nonparametric causal effect estimation without global structure learning.

problem: Multi-objective generation with Generative Flow Networks requires joint training for each objective combination, meaning any change to objectives necessitates retraining from scratch.
approach: Compose pre-trained GFlowNets at inference time to handle diverse reward combinations from linear scalarization to complex nonlinear operators without fine-tuning.
contribution: Framework achieves performance comparable to baselines on molecule generation while enabling rapid adaptation to new objective sets; exactly recovers target for linear scalarization.

problem: Repeating smaller datasets can speed up training compared to larger datasets, a 'small-vs-large gap' observed across tasks but not explained by existing theory.
approach: Argue that speedup comes from appropriate layer-wise growth enabled by sampling biases, which is more pronounced with smaller dataset size, supported by theoretical and empirical analysis.
contribution: Smaller datasets with more repetitions can be proactively leveraged as favorable inductive biases for optimization, particularly in reasoning tasks.

problem: Unified discrete frameworks for vision-language-action policies lag behind decoupled continuous designs due to limitations in action chunking and temporal modeling.
approach: RoboOmni treats actions as discrete modality with Multi-Token Action Prediction (MTAP), integrating action chunking directly into tokenizer while preserving native VLM training.
contribution: RoboOmni establishes state-of-the-art performance on CALVIN and SimplerEnv, achieving 94.4% average success rate with FAST tokenizer and 27x inference speedup.

problem: Standard LiDAR semi-supervised learning generates pseudo-labels from a single source, reinforcing confirmation bias and propagating errors during training.
approach: CoLLiS trains multiple LiDAR representations collaboratively as coequal students, each adaptively distilled from multiple sources while monitoring inter-student disparities to resolve contradictory supervision.
contribution: CoLLiS consistently outperforms state-of-the-art LiDAR SemiSL methods with particularly strong gains in low-label regimes by mitigating confirmation bias.

problem: Personalized federated learning collaboration graphs can drift into degenerate regimes—either global consensus or spontaneous clustering—without constraints on collaboration geometry.
approach: pFedCCG preserves expressivity via controlled collaboration geometry by building similarity-based templates, optimizing Markovian collaboration matrices with prescribed distributions, and scheduling collaboration strength.
contribution: pFedCCG achieves consistent personalization gains across heterogeneity settings and markedly reduces collapse and self-clustering compared to unconstrained collaboration.

problem: Large Reasoning Models exhibit over-thinking issues because RLVR methods choose outcome-correct trajectories, reinforcing redundant explorations in long chain-of-thoughts.
approach: ThoughtFold uses introspective preference learning to identify redundancy within correct trajectories, yielding masked preference optimization that penalizes redundant explorations.
contribution: ThoughtFold reduces token usage of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B by approximately 56% while maintaining state-of-the-art accuracy.

problem: Current off-policy unsupervised reinforcement learning methods are limited by non-stationarity of skill semantics and brittle generalization to downstream tasks.
approach: GenDa introduces skill relabeling to mitigate non-stationarity and Complementary Information Bottleneck (CIB) to encourage focus on ego-centric features robust to distribution shifts.
contribution: GenDa significantly enhances scalability of URL with superior generality and sample efficiency for downstream task performance.
